newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's farmers in disarray after blockades, snub.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's farmers in disarray after blockades, snub.

text.p: Hungarian farmers who have blocked roads in protest against tax changes were in disarray on Thursday after snubbing the prime minister and failing to convince other farmers to join them.
Hungarian radio said the farmers continued to block roads. But they have failed to convince the majority of the country's 1.5 million farmers to join them.

The protest leaders, based in the central Hungarian town of Kiskoros, failed to show up for a meeting with Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Wednesday night. Horn promptly called off any further talks with the Kiskoros farmers, who have set up an organisation called METESZ.
However, another farm organisation, MAGOSZ, said it planned to start its own protests on Monday.

METESZ began its protests demanding that the government roll back requirements that farmers start making social security payments and keep thorough accounts. Its protests widened later to include the entire government farm policy.
Before coming to power in 1994, Horn's Socialist Party promised to streamline Hungarian farming, but it has yet to deliver.

Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy, who has admitted that Hungary's agriculture is in crisis, presented the first draft of a medium-term farming policy on Thursday but details were likely to emerge only on Friday.
That is cold comfort for the tens of thousands of farmers who have been trying to survive under increasingly untenable conditions.
Kiskoros farmers first blocked roads on February 24 in a protest against the new farm taxation policy. The Socialist-Free Democrat coalition accepted most of their original claims.
However, the government has since taken a tougher stance, refusing further concessions to farmers who they said already pay less taxes than other citizens.
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy warned on Wednesday he would remain in his post only as long as no concessions were made to "preferred social sectors".
Horn now seems determined to back Medgyessy, the third Finance Minister since the coalition came to power in 1994.
The Kiskoros protesters refused to meet Horn on Wednesday after farmer leader Gyula Kosa said talks with ministry officials showed the government was not prepared to make concessions.
